title: Dynamics 365 Sales: run multiple Sales Qualification Agents in one environment
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, administrative controls and agent-state API are supported. The Sales billing page still describes messages, while Copilot Studio licensing says the currency changed to Copilot Credits; acknowledge this documentation difference.

claims.claim: Sales Qualification Agent is an AI agent that researches leads.
claims.quote: Sales Qualification Agent in Dynamics 365 Sales is an AI agent that automates lead qualification.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Research and engage mode autonomously sends outreach emails.
claims.quote: In this mode, the agent autonomously sends outreach emails to leads and engages with them based on their responses.

claims.claim: Research and engage mode sends follow-up emails.
claims.quote: | Send follow-up emails and clarify questions | ❌ | ✅ |

claims.claim: Research and engage mode evaluates lead fit.
claims.quote: the agent autonomously engages with each lead, follows up, and evaluates fit based on your seller hand-off rules

claims.claim: Promising leads are handed over to sellers.
claims.quote: Leads that demonstrate purchase intent and meet most of your criteria are handed over to sellers for qualification

claims.claim: Research and engage mode can disqualify leads.
claims.quote: Leads that demonstrate purchase intent and meet most of your criteria are handed over to sellers for qualification, while those that don’t are disqualified

claims.claim: Learn has no page describing configuration of several Sales Qualification Agents, including inter-agent priority and fallback, at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sales Qualification" "multiple agents" routing fallback priority; opened Learn's configure-sales-qualification-agent, selection criteria, assignment rules, import-export-agent-solutions and msdyn_salesagentprofile reference. No multi-agent configuration found.

claims.claim: The selection criteria page says the agent segment priority is always low and one above the default segment.
claims.quote: The priority of the segment created for the agent is always low and one above the default segment.

claims.claim: An overlap with seller work-assignment segments sends leads to sellers instead of the agent.
claims.quote: ensure that the segment you're creating for the agent doesn't overlap with the segments used for work assignment to sellers. If there's an overlap, leads are assigned to sellers instead of the agent.

claims.claim: The import page refers to agent profiles and recommends one solution per profile.
claims.quote: Create one solution per agent profile to ensure each profile can be packaged and deployed independently.

claims.claim: Selection criteria assign leads to an agent, while assignment rules hand processed leads to sellers or teams.
claims.quote:
Configure selection criteria for the agent process the leads.
Configure assignment rules for the agent to assign processed leads to the appropriate sellers.

claims.claim: No source says existing single-agent setups change without action.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sales Qualification Agent" "multiple" "environment"; opened Learn's overview, setup, settings, start-agent and import-export-agent-solutions pages. No automatic migration or change to existing setups was stated.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The capability is admin-opt-in because an administrator must configure an agent before sellers can use it.
claims.quote: As an admin, you need to set up the Sales Qualification Agent before your sellers can use it for lead research, target customer profile assessment, and initial email outreach.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Sales Qualification Agent uses tenant capacity to process leads and generate insights.
claims.quote: The Sales Qualification Agent uses the capacity assigned to your tenant to process leads and generate insights.

claims.claim: The setup page lists a Copilot Studio license as a prerequisite and links to Copilot Studio licensing.
claims.quote: You have a Copilot Studio license. Learn more in Copilot Studio licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption-based.
claims.quote: Selected Copilot and agent capabilities in Dynamics 365 Sales use consumption-based billing, charging per use.

claims.claim: Direct cost is variable because agent usage is metered.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go model charges for the actual number of messages consumed by agents during the month.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Prepaid capacity is available through Copilot Studio message packs according to the Sales billing page.
claims.quote: The prepaid capacity model uses Copilot Studio message pack subscriptions

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The agent supports pay-as-you-go capacity.
claims.quote: You can set up either prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go capacity for the agent.

claims.claim: Both billing models require linking the Dynamics 365 Sales environment to a Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: Both models require that you link your Dynamics 365 Sales environment to a Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity is consumed first when both models are used.
claims.quote: Both billing models can be used on the Dynamics 365 Sales environment. Prepaid capacity is consumed first.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Sales billing page describes Microsoft Copilot Studio messages as the billing unit.
claims.quote: These capabilities use Microsoft Copilot Studio messages for AI interactions and tasks, like retrieving information and responding to prompts. Messages are the billing units that measure usage.
claims.fix: After the Meter paragraph add: "The Sales billing page still uses messages terminology; Copilot Studio licensing says the common currency changed from messages to Copilot Credits on September 1, 2025, with no change in the quantity per prepaid pack or pay-as-you-go rate." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing in sources. Keep the existing attribution to the Sales billing page.

claims.claim: The Sales billing page points to the Power Platform Licensing Guide for billing and rates.
claims.quote: Learn more about billing and rates in Power Platform Licensing Guide.

claims.claim: The Sales billing page says depleted quota makes the AI capability unavailable until capacity is added.
claims.quote: When the quota is depleted, the AI capability is unavailable until more capacity is added.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Sales sends in-app notifications when capacity is low or depleted.
claims.quote: If your organization's quota is low or depleted, users receive in-app notifications about the status and necessary actions.

claims.claim: For pay-as-you-go the Sales billing page directs administrators to Microsoft Cost Management in Azure to view usage and adjust budgets.
claims.quote: For pay-as-you-go, use Microsoft Cost Management in the Azure portal to view detailed usage and adjust spending limits (budgets) to free up more capacity.

claims.claim: Research and engage mode requires a shared mailbox.
claims.quote: | Create a shared mailbox | Research and engage | The agent mailbox that you use to send emails and follow-ups in compliance with your org’s policies.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Scope
claims.claim: Research and engage mode requires server-side synchronization between Dynamics 365 Sales and Exchange.
claims.quote: | Configuring server-side synchronization | Research and engage | Connect Dynamics 365 Sales and Exchange to sync emails, contacts, tasks, and calendar.

claims.claim: The common Sales-agent prerequisites are a one-time setup.
claims.quote: To set up and use the built-in sales agents such as the Sales Qualification Agent and Sales Close Agent, make sure you meet certain common prerequisites. This is a one-time setup.

claims.claim: The common prerequisites direct administrators to accept data movement under Generative AI features > Move data across regions in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Move data across regions: Select Accept terms to open the Power Platform admin center and allow data movement under Generative AI features > Move data across regions.

claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive knowledge connector is required when the agent uses those internal documents for enrichment.
claims.quote: | Knowledge source with SharePoint or OneDrive | Required only if the agent is configured to use internal documents on SharePoint or OneDrive for enrichment. |

claims.claim: Setup includes creating an application in Azure.
claims.quote: You need an Azure AD application to securely authenticate the agent’s Dataverse Application User, so it can act independently through app-based access.

claims.claim: Setup includes a Dataverse application user with the AISalesPerson role.
claims.quote: Create an app user in Dataverse and assign AISalesPerson role

claims.claim: The app user lets the agent act independently, including sending emails and owning records.
claims.quote: Create a Dataverse app user so the agent can act independently, like send emails, own records, and more.

claims.claim: A newly created lead's owner must not be the app user used to create the agent.
claims.quote: When new leads are created, ensure that the lead owner is not the app user used to create the agent.

claims.claim: Stopping an agent retains its configuration rather than deleting it.
claims.quote: Stopping the agent doesn’t delete it and retains the configuration settings.

claims.claim: Stopping an agent prevents processing of new leads.
claims.quote: However, new leads and leads that are in process will not be processed.

claims.claim: The manage page says in-process leads stop, while the setup page says existing orchestration continues to seller handover or supervisor review.
claims.quote: Existing leads which are already in pipeline (orchestration), will continue until the lead is either handed over to a seller or added to the supervisor dashboard for next steps.

claims.claim: Already processed leads remain available after the agent is stopped.
claims.quote: Leads that are already processed will continue to be available in the application.

claims.claim: A configured and started agent cannot be deleted without contacting Microsoft Support.
claims.quote: Once you configure and start an agent, it can’t be deleted. If you want to delete the agent, contact Microsoft Support.

claims.claim: Updated settings apply to new leads.
claims.quote: The updated agent is active, and new leads are processed based on the updated settings.

claims.claim: Leads processed using earlier configuration are not reprocessed after editing.
claims.quote: leads that are already processed based on the previous agent configurations will not be reprocessed

claims.quote: Searched: "Dynamics 365 Sales" "AI Agents" setting API PowerShell Power Platform; "AI Agents" "Sales" "Set-TenantSettings" "d365Sales"; "D365SalesAIAgents"; "d365Sales_AIAgents". Opened Learn's copilot-hub and prerequisites-for-all-agents; no equivalent operation found.

claims.claim: The tenant administrator's environment or environment-group switch covers out-of-the-box Sales AI agents and turns their Dynamics 365 Sales features off when disabled.
claims.quote: As a tenant administrator, you can turn on or off AI capabilities such as Copilot and AI agents in Dynamics 365 Sales, across environments, and environment groups.

claims.claim: The broad Sales AI capabilities switch is on by default in all environments.
claims.quote: By default, the AI capabilities are turned on in all environments. If you turn off the capability, the features are turned off automatically in Dynamics 365 Sales.

claims.claim: Supervisor lead views are also available to sellers unless EnableRoleBasedSystemViews is true.

claims.claim: Agent creation starts in the AI hub's Agent manager, with Research selected and Engage added for autonomous engagement.
claims.quote:
In the Agent manager section, select Create and manage agent.
Research is selected by default and is non-editable. You can add engage capabilities to the agent by selecting Engage.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing on a small scale before the production scenario.
claims.quote: We recommend that you test the agent's functionality on a smaller scale before testing it for your production scenario.
